description: San Francisco residents' trip mode shares (all trips and NON-WORK trips) by home area within SF and by household income, plus related evidence (transit-use frequency by district/neighborhood, Muni rider income/purpose, BATS 2019/2023 SF mode shares by income, low-income fare programs). Assembled to test whether non-work transit use varies by neighborhood/income beyond what commute shares capture. Survey-derived numbers are either (a) transcribed from published tables/dashboard extracts exactly as published, or (b) tabulated by us from public respondent-level files (SFMTA Travel Decision Survey; SF City Survey) with the scripts named below; (b) values are labeled 'tabulated' and carry sample sizes and, for TDS transit shares, respondent-clustered standard errors. Nothing is extrapolated.
headline: No public post-2015 source gives SF-resident NON-WORK mode shares by sub-city home area except the SFMTA Travel Decision Survey (TDS) respondent files (2017, 2019, 2021; ~400-470 SF adult respondents and ~2,300-2,800 trips each; 5 ZIP-based home zones). BATS 2023 is public only at county x income (dashboard); its microdata require an MTC NDA. The 2017 NHTS California add-on may allow tract-level tabulation after free NREL TSDC registration (not done; unverified).

TDS pooled 2017+2019 (pre-COVID), non-work trips, public transit share: SOUTHEAST Zone 5 (94112/94124/94134) 16.6% (SE 3.0) vs WEST Zones 3+4 (Richmond/Sunset/Parkside/West Portal) 13.8% (SE 2.4); Zone 1 (Mission/SoMa/Potrero/Castro) 17.9% (2.5); Zone 2 (downtown/NE) 19.5% (2.5). Area differences are within ~1 SE.

Income dominates: TDS pooled 2017+2019 non-work transit share is 29.2% for households <$75k vs 9.2% for >=$75k; <$35k 39.5%, >$200k 5.3%. The gap holds within every zone (SE Z5: 24.3% vs 5.3%; WEST Z3+Z4: 27.9% vs 6.7%; Z1: 33.9% vs 9.6%).
BATS (MTC dashboard, linked weekday trips, SF adults): transit share 2023 = 18.2% (<$50k), 16.9% ($50-100k), 11.1% ($100-200k), 10.9% (>=$200k); 2019 = 23.3%, 14.7%, 17.4%, 13.1%.

SF City Survey (respondent-level, DataSF): share using public transit 3+ days/week in 2023: <$50k 55.3% vs >$200k 20.4%. 2026 neighborhoods: Excelsior 50.5%, Mission 47.4%, Visitacion Valley 43.9% (n=27), Portola 43.2%, Bayview-Hunters Point 34.1%; Sunset/Parkside 30.5%, Inner Richmond 27.3%, Outer Richmond 27.4%, Inner Sunset 46.5%.

sources.name: SFCTA SF-CHAMP documentation (sfcta/sfchampdocs)
sources.provides: Model structure only. Calibration sections link to an internal intranet (intranet2.sfcta.org); no public district-level mode share targets found. Public docs state DaySim cost coefficient = BaseCostPerDollar / (HH_income/30000)^CostIncomePower with CostIncomePower_Work 0.6 and CostIncomePower_Other 0.5 (activity_demand_models.rst), i.e. SF-CHAMP's non-work mode choice is income-sensitive through cost.

tdsTabulated.status: tabulated by us from respondent-level files; scripts data/beta3/raw/mode-by-area/tds_load.py + tds_tables.py
method: Universe: SF-resident respondents (Q2=9), all trips made yesterday and two days ago (Q4*/Q5* series), anywhere; each trip weighted by the respondent WEIGHT. Trips with no recorded mode dropped (42 in 2019, 4 in 2021).

Validation against the published 2019 report (SF residents, page 6): tabulated transit 17.2% vs published public transit 17%; walk 24.6% vs 25%; drove alone + drove with others 48.1% vs 48%. 2021: transit 9.7% vs 10%, walk 29.1% vs 29%.

Purpose classes: 'work' = destination purpose Work, or destination Home with previous destination Work (same day). 'nonWork' = all other trips (school, shopping/errands, social/eat out/recreation, escort, other, and home-bound trips not following a work stop).

Mode: publicTransit = 'Public transportation, such as Muni, BART, Caltrain, ferry or public bus' (BART/Caltrain are included; cannot be separated). privateShuttle separate. drivePct = drove alone + drove with others + car share. 2021 allowed up to 3 modes per trip; 14 of 2,487 trips had 2 modes and were coded transit if any mode was transit, else first mode.
Income: 2017/2019 Q29/Q30 bins (<=$35k, $35-75k, $75-100k, $100-200k, >$200k); 2021 Q36 finer bins aggregated to the same breaks. income2 = <$75k vs >=$75k.
publicTransitSEpct: respondent-clustered linearization SE of the weighted ratio (trips are clustered within respondents; the published report ignores clustering).
2021 is mid-COVID (May-Sep 2021); 2017+2019 pooled is the pre-COVID estimate with the largest sample.

zoneDefinitions.source: TDS_2021_Data.xlsx sheet 'Zone Description'; 2017 and 2019 ZONE codes cross-checked against home ZIP (Q25A-SF) and are identical

groups.note: Mission (94110) is in Z1 with SoMa, Potrero/Dogpatch, Castro, Mission Bay. Z4 includes Glen Park/Diamond Heights (94131) and West Portal (94127). Z5 also contains 94188 respondents in 2019 (1).

tdsPublished.note: Published tables combine SF-resident and non-resident trips to/from/within SF assuming 73%/27% (SF-CHAMP 2015). Not SF-resident-only. Percent as printed.
tdsPublished.pageNote: Page numbers are PDF pages as extracted (2019 report p.8 'Trips By Income'; 2021 report p.7 table following the age table).

batsDashboardSF.status: exact values from the published Tableau extract (summarize_BATS_TripLevel_Share_2019_2023_for_dashboard), SF home county rows
batsDashboardSF.definition: Weighted share of weekday (Mon-Thu) trips by SF-resident persons, linked trips (mode_label uses WALKTRAN/DRIVETRAN). '18 and over' rows are what the dashboard shows. Shares are fractions. mode5cat_label (Drive Alone, Drive with Others, Transit, Walk, Bike) sums to 1 over those five groups only, i.e. its denominator excludes TNC, school bus and other (smaller totalUnweightedTrips); mode_label (10 modes) sums to 1 over all trips. Headline transit shares quote mode5cat.
batsDashboardSF.caution: Some tiny DRIVETRAN/SCHBUS shares are stored in the source as values like 6.3e-05; 'Poor' reliability rows are flagged as in the source.
